Thus, while histopathology is definitive, the pre-biopsy evidence overwhelmingly favors **phyllodes tumor**, with benign or borderline subtype most likely given lack of overt cytologic atypia, mitotic activity, or infiltrative margins (which cannot be assessed radiologically but are absent from reported features).

[EVIDENCE]  
- Rapidly enlarging left breast mass over 4 weeks  
- Mass size >5 cm (5.9 × 4.3 × 3.8 cm on US; 6.1 × 4.4 × 3.9 cm on MRI)  
- Well-circumscribed, polylobulated morphology on both ultrasound and mammography  
- Internal echogenic septations on ultrasound  
- T2-hyperintense, non-mass-like, lobulated lesion on MRI  
- Homogeneous mild-to-moderate contrast enhancement without washout on MRI  
- Absence of Doppler vascularity within the mass  
- Absence of microcalcifications, posterior acoustic shadowing/enhancement, or spiculation  
- No skin changes, nipple discharge, retraction, or axillary lymphadenopathy  
- Normal CRP, ESR, CA 15-3, CA 125, and CEA  

[GAPS]  
- Histopathologic assessment of stromal cellularity, atypia, mitotic count, and margin infiltration (required to grade phyllodes tumor as benign/borderline/malignant)  
- Immunohistochemical staining (e.g., CD34, Ki-67, p53) to support stromal proliferation and rule out mimics  
- Evaluation of epithelial component integrity (e.g., clefting vs. true stromal overgrowth)  
- Absence of reported gross or microscopic necrosis or infiltrative margins  

[DIAGNOSIS]  
Phyllodes tumor
